evals.prompt: Draft a design doc for a notification service that consumes domain events and delivers email and push notifications for about 1M events/day.
assertions: Non-goals are real scope boundaries a reader might otherwise assume are in scope, not throat-clearing
Each alternative carries a two-sentence what-it-is and why-we-didn't-pick-it
Every risk has a mitigation, not a bare list of concerns
Goals are stated with measurable targets rather than adjectives
The rollout section names stages and what would halt it
Facts not supplied by the user are marked as open questions rather than invented

evals.prompt: Can you write the design doc for offline mode in the inspector app? Product's brief is brief.md and Halvard's notes from our eng discussion are eng-notes.md. It goes to design review on Thursday so it needs to stand on its own. Please include how much storage it needs per device too.
assertions: It flags that the timeline does not work as written: 14 weeks from a 14 Dec 2026 start ends around 22 March 2027, after the 1 March 2027 Calder County deadline, and it proposes a way through or raises it as a decision
The size of the problem is given as 1,120 of 8,400 inspections (about 13%) with sync or save errors, or the brief's 'around 40%' is called out as unsupported by the logged numbers
It does not apply plain last-write-wins to signed inspections; it surfaces the conflict between the brief and the compliance rule that a signed inspection must never be overwritten
The server-side sync endpoint is shown as depending on the Platform team with no owner confirmed and nobody yet asked
Per-device storage need is stated as not yet measured, with no invented figure, and measuring it is listed as a to-do or open question
At least two of the alternatives from the notes (outbox queue, CRDT library, PDF re-keying) are described with the reason each was not chosen as the main approach
The rollout starts with the 12 Calder County volunteers and gives at least one concrete, checkable condition for widening or stopping it
It does not invent crash rates, backend load figures, costs or device counts that are not in the two files

evals.prompt: need a one-pager design doc by end of day for moving our cron jobs off the old box. there's like 30ish of them on a single ec2 instance (cron-01), some of them nobody knows what they do anymore. thinking either k8s cronjobs since we already have a cluster, or some managed scheduler. Jonas wants it done before the OS on that instance goes end of life but I don't remember the date. 4 of us on the team.
assertions: It delivers a design doc in the reply rather than only asking questions
The OS end-of-life date is recorded as unknown and to be confirmed; no specific date is invented
The jobs nobody understands are dealt with explicitly, through an inventory or audit step or a named risk with a mitigation, not assumed to be understood
Both Kubernetes CronJobs and a managed scheduler are described, with a reason for preferring one or a statement of what would decide it
The job count stays approximate ('about 30'); it does not invent an exact count, job names, schedules or failure rates
It says how a migrated job is checked before its old cron entry is removed, and how to go back if it misbehaves
It is about one page: roughly 700 words or fewer
